The after initial_prompt_points now has exactly 10 centres for 10 rings (8 midpoint + 2 assume) instead of 11, so the extra intersection is gone and the prompt grid is regular. The current detected_lines.png is cleaner but still carries spurious lines: a red oblique segment inside the top rail/invert band (x~1900-2100, y~50), oblique segments that cut across bolt-hole rows in the dense right half (e.g. x~1200-1450 y~1530, x~1700-1950 y~2380), and dense blue horizontal fallback lines in the top and bottom rail bands (y<100, y>2900) plus isolated horizontals in the sparse left third that sit on nothing. The two rounds so far form a monotone response on this subset: adding lines (round 1) cost -0.137 F1, removing lines (round 2) gained +0.059 F1, with fill/ring/nan essentially flat both times.

proposal.rationale: Final round: take one more step along the direction that was just accepted (ontology r_tighten_hough), sized like round 2 but stopping short of the bound edges so genuine joint lines are not eliminated entirely: binary_threshold 145 -> 155 to drop more weak outlier pixels in the rail bands, hough_threshold_oblique 60 -> 72 and maxLineGap_oblique 30 -> 22 so oblique segments need denser contiguous support and cannot bridge bolt-hole rows, hough_threshold_horizontal 80 -> 88 to thin the horizontal fallback lines that carpet the top/bottom rail bands. Prompt-centre count is already anchored at 10 by the unchanged vertical Hough and by midpoint/assume fallback, so the risk to ring_count_error is low; SAM fill barely moved under round 2 and is expected to stay near 0.735. Unfolding untouched (stage-1 locked); denoising, enhancing and sam untouched because their measurements are healthy and round 1/2 showed detection-only overlays move F1 without disturbing them. All values are within configs/bounds/staggered.json.
